chunks: the neglecting by a man of what he has been made responsible for and doing what is to be done by others is a manifest weakness and a ruinous sight.

Certainly, your advance on the people of Qarqīsiyā, and your leaving the arsenals over which we had set you, without anyone to protect them or to repulse the enemy force, savoured of shattered thinking.
In this way, you served like a bridge for the enemy who came marauding on your allies

while your arms were weak, you had no awe around you; you could not prevent the enemy from advancing; you could not break his might; you could not defend the people of your area and you could not discharge functions on behalf of your Imām.
ai.seo_question: What were the main criticisms Imam Ali leveled against Kumayl ibn al-Harith regarding his governance?
ai.summary: In this letter, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) critiques Kumayl ibn al-Harith for his strategic incompetence, specifically noting how his aggressive but ill-timed raid on Qarqisiya left the arsenals undefended, turning him into a bridge for enemy incursions rather than a shield. This passage is historically significant as it illustrates the Imam’s emphasis on administrative accountability and the principle that mismanagement of entrusted resources constitutes a clear sign of flawed judgment ('ra'y mutabbar'). It serves as a foundational text in Shia political ethics regarding the qualifications of governors.
